newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas falls but market remains thin and quiet.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas falls but market remains thin and quiet.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures closed lower on Monday , but trade was only seen in three of the twelve monthly contracts and the market remained thin and illiquid.
"I'm afraid the IPE needs a much greater volume for meaningful commentary," said a broker.
A total of 120 lots were traded over the day, a significant improvement from the morning session when only ten lots - representing a mere two deals - were struck.
A broker added that before the market starts to take off, all players so far qualified to participate must start to do so regularly, and not all are doing this yet.
"Then they'll draw in more players who are not yet qualified," he said. But at the moment bids and offers are too far apart. "It needs bids and offers with corresponding size closer to market value."

March traded 35 lots, representing 35,000 therms a day for the month, with the lowest trade of the day, at 11.96 pence a therm, done a minute before the contract closed at 1600 GMT. This is a fall of 0.180 pence a therm from the previous settlement price of 12.14 pence a therm.

The only other month with any liquidity was August, which saw 80 lots traded. This month also closed at the day's low, 11.40 pence a therm, down by 0.10 pence a therm from Friday's settlement of 11.50 pence.
